stem: A nurse manager uses a servant-leadership approach. Which behavior best reflects this leadership style?

options.A: Centralize important decisions and limit staff participation because servant leadership depends on clear control by the formal leader.
options.B: Prioritize the leader’s recognition over team development when the two goals conflict because status reinforces authority.
options.C: Support staff growth and well-being, share in decision-making, and develop team members toward their highest potential.
options.D: Avoid difficult leadership decisions and transfer responsibility for unit outcomes to frontline staff so the leader does not dominate.

rationale: Open RN's leadership-style table describes servant leaders as focusing on the growth and well-being of team members, sharing in decision-making, and developing team members to their highest potential. C directly matches those characteristics.
educational_objective: Identify servant leadership by its focus on team-member growth and well-being, shared decision-making, and development of others.

source_original.stem: A nurse manager uses a servant-leadership approach. Which behavior best reflects this leadership style?

options.A: Centralize important decisions and limit staff participation because servant leadership depends on clear control by the formal leader.
options.B: Prioritize the leader’s recognition over team development when the two goals conflict because status reinforces authority.
options.C: Support staff growth and well-being, share appropriately in decisions, and develop team members while remaining accountable for leadership outcomes.
options.D: Avoid difficult leadership decisions and transfer responsibility for unit outcomes to frontline staff so the leader does not dominate.

source_original.rationale: Open RN describes servant leadership as focusing on growth and well-being of team members, sharing decision-making, and developing team members to their highest potential.
source_original.source_detail: Table 4.2b, Characteristics of Leadership Styles — Servant row. Open RN 2nd edition, 2024; NCBI Bookshelf currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Management of Care, printed p.7: advocacy/client rights, prioritization, quality improvement, interdisciplinary collaboration, informed consent, legal scope and plan-of-care activities. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the servant-leadership construct and key C, removed the added accountability clause not needed to identify the style, aligned the final option exactly with Open RN Table 4.2b, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: NCBI/Open RN nursing-management textbook; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: 2024 second edition live on NCBI and rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final keyed behavior now tracks the source characteristics directly without adding a separate accountability proposition.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect; centralized control characterizes authoritarian leadership more than servant leadership.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; servant leadership centers team growth/well-being rather than leader status.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect; servant leadership is not passive avoidance or abandonment of leadership decisions.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C contains all three source-defined servant characteristics.
audit_findings.cueing: Options are leadership behaviors of comparable form.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read Table 4.2b, all options, rationale, objective and NCSBN Management mapping. C remained uniquely correct.
